Here's the SKILL.md as requested:

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Use for anything related to our company.
---

# Company Handbook

## 1. Code Style
### 1.1 Python
### 1.2 TypeScript

## 2. Deploy Process
### 2.1 Service A: deploy / rollback
### 2.2 Service B: deploy / rollback
### 2.3 Service C: deploy / rollback
### 2.4 Service D: deploy / rollback

## 3. On-Call Runbook
### 3.1 How to use this runbook
### 3.2 Alerts (35 entries: symptom, triage, fix, escalation)

## 4. PTO and Expense Policy
### 4.1 PTO
### 4.2 Expenses

## 5. Brand Voice Guide

## 6. Org Chart

## 7. Glossary
```

Paste each section's content under its heading and you're done.

**Before you ship it, three things you should know.** None of them requires changing the "one skill" plan.

1. **The description will hurt triggering.** Claude decides whether to load a skill from its description alone. "Anything related to our company" gives it nothing to match against, so the skill will load unpredictably: sometimes for unrelated work, often not when someone asks about a deploy rollback or a specific alert. A drop-in replacement that's still one line:

   > `description: Company handbook covering Python/TypeScript code style, deploy and rollback steps for our 4 services, on-call alert runbook, PTO and expense policy, marketing brand voice, org chart, and internal glossary. Use when writing code, deploying, responding to alerts, answering HR/policy questions, writing marketing copy, or looking up people or internal terms.`

2. **3,000 lines will load all at once.** When the skill triggers, the whole SKILL.md enters context. A question about PTO would pull in 900 lines of runbook too. Guidance is to keep SKILL.md under about 500 lines. The low-effort fix keeps it one skill and one folder: put each section in its own file (`runbook.md`, `deploy.md`, etc.) next to SKILL.md, and make each body section a one-line pointer like "For alerts, read runbook.md." You'd still maintain one skill, and Claude only reads the part it needs. This is about 15 minutes of extra work.

3. **Phone numbers.** Skill files tend to get committed to repos and shared widely. Check whether personal phone numbers should be in there, or whether names, roles, and a link to the HR directory would be enough.

If you want, I can write the split-file version so you have it ready to show your lead alongside this one.
